item.title: Bob Boone has passed away at age 78
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PA - CIRCA 1980: Catcher Bob Boone #8 of the Philadelphia Phillies in action during an Major League Baseball game circa 1980 at Veterans Stadium in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Boone played for the Phillies from 1972-81. (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bob Boone, longtime major league catcher and manager, has passed away, per reports. He was 78. Boone spent 19 years in the major leagues. Drafted out of Stanford by the Philadelphia Phillies in 1969, Boone got a cup of coffee in 1972 before becoming the Phillies’ regular catcher in 1973. He finished third in the National League Rookie of the Year voting that season, tied with Dan Driessen and Elias Sosa, with Gary Matthews finishing first and Steve Rogers second in what was an especially strong class, which also saw Ron Cey, Johnny Grubb, Davey Lopez and Richie Zisk receive votes. Boone was his team’s starting catcher every season from 1973 through 1989, when he caught an American League high 129 games at the age of 41 for the Kansas City Royals while winning his 12th Gold Glove. Boone was remarkably durable, even as he aged — he caught 121 games for the Angels in 1988 in his age 40 season, and is the only player to have caught at least 120 games in a season in his 40s. There have been just five seasons in major league history where a player who is 38 or older has caught at least 120 games in a season — Carlton Fisk, in 1987, at the age of 39, and Boone’s age 38-41 seasons. Boone was a fixture behind the plate for the Phillies for almost a decade, including their three straight division title teams from 1976-78, as well as the 1980 team that beat the Kansas City Royals in the World Series for the Phillies’ first ever World Series title. Despite his being an excellent defensive catcher, the play he’s best known for is a dropped foul pop up in Game 6 of the World Series that Pete Rose snagged before it hit the ground: Boone was acquired by the California Angels, another team striving to win their first World Series, after the 1981 season. He spent the next seven seasons as the Angels’ primary catcher, with the Angels advancing to the ALCS in 1982 and 1986. Boone was behind the plate when the Mike Witt and Donnie Moore each gave up two runs homers in the top of the ninth of Game 5 of the ALCS, turning a 5-2 Angels lead into a 6-5 deficit, and then led off the bottom of the ninth with a single that led to pinch runner Ruppert Jones scoring the tying run that sent the game into extra innings.* * Boone’s replacement behind the plate was the Angels’ backup catcher, and future Rangers coach and manager, Jerry Narron. Had the Angels won that game, they would have advanced to play the New York Mets in the World Series. Instead, Dave Henderson, who homered off of Moore in the ninth, hit a sacrifice fly off of Moore in the 11th to give the Red Sox a 7-6 lead. item.description: Marnus Labuschagne is refusing to let his latest Test setback dent his confidence, insisting he has no doubt about returning to the Australian side after being dropped for the upcoming World Test Championship series against New Zealand. The 32-year-old, however, is ready to put the scrutiny behind him for now, shifting his focus to domestic cricket and helping Queensland win games in the Sheffield Shield. Labuschagne's omission comes after a prolonged lean patch in Test cricket, with the right-hander struggling to rediscover the consistency that once made him one of Australia's most dependable batters. Despite the disappointment, he believes a return to domestic cricket will give him the opportunity to regain his rhythm and put himself back in contention for national selection. Speaking at the Gabba ahead of Queensland's Sheffield Shield clash, Labuschagne acknowledged the pressure he has been under over the past couple of years and said he intends to use this period to enjoy his cricket again. "You are pretty aware as a cricketer ... you use this as an opportunity to step back from the scrutiny, and being under the pump for probably two years now,” Labuschagne told the media on Tuesday, as quoted by Fox Sports. “You take this opportunity to come back and play for Queensland, enjoy your time here and find ways to win games for Queensland. Score runs, enjoy the games and I think my path back to the Australian team will work itself out." 'No doubt I will be back': Labuschagne backs himself for Australia return The Australian batter has experienced a similar setback before. He was left out of the squad for Australia's tour of the West Indies last year but responded emphatically, scoring five centuries across red-ball and white-ball cricket for Queensland in eight innings to force his way back into the national setup ahead of the home Ashes series against England. Drawing confidence from that experience, Labuschagne remains optimistic about earning another opportunity, although he admitted that he does not know when the recall could come. "I have done it before, and I have got no doubt I will be back there. When? Who knows, but that is the aspiration and desire. Right now, my feet are firmly fixed here with Queensland and doing whatever I can as a captain, batter, in the field and with the ball to help us win games," he added. item.title: Cowboys proved they don't have to blow every close game, here's what we learned
item.description: The Dallas Cowboys survived a game they could have given away . Giving away close games is becoming a theme for the 2026 Dallas Cowboys. They couldn’t score a touchdown against the Baltimore Ravens in a goal-to-go situation at the end of that contest. Then they gave up a game-winning field goal when, at the kickoff, they had seven seconds left. They lost to an undrafted free agent rookie quarterback at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Dallas blew a 14-point fourth-quarter lead at AT&T Stadium for the first time in team history to the Arizona Cardinals , and the Colts led 23-20 with under two minutes to go in the game. The Brian Schottenheimer era has been plagued by inconsistent, self-inflicted issues that keep opponents close only for the game to slip away late. This time, the defense stood up enough for Dak Prescott to drag the team to a late victory despite losing the turnover battle and committing 14 penalties for 153 yards. It’s only the second win under Schottenheimer in which the team scores fewer than 30 points. There is no such thing as a bad win for a team still able to take their division. Dallas needs to take what they learned from this game and try to start the second winning streak of Schottenheimer’s head-coaching tenure. The defense can win Dallas a game For the first time in a full four quarters, the Dallas defense was the best part of the team. The special teams kicked a ball out of bounds and missed a go-ahead field goal in the fourth quarter. The offense had two turnovers, one that gave the Indianapolis offense the ball in the red zone, and allowed the Colts to stay in the game with poor play for the first two and a half quarters. Without starters DeMarvion Overshown and Joey Porter Jr. , the Cowboys' defense forced five three-and-outs, including three straight in the second quarter. They allowed under five yards per pass, a 23% conversion rate on third down, and held Jonathan Taylor to 46 yards on 13 attempts with zero explosive runs. Dallas had a defensive-led victory for the first time in multiple seasons. He had a 25% explosive-play percentage, and that is a dynamic the Dallas offense desperately needs in the run game. item.title: Denny Hamlin Wins Stage, Loses NASCAR Championship
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Denny Hamlin finished third in the final standings after leading more than 1,000 laps during the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series season. The 45-year-old driver crossed the finish line in sixth place at Homestead-Miami Speedway on Sunday night. He had four victories and never failed to finish a single race due to a crash or mechanical issue. Yet the trophy went to Kyle Larson instead. The race served as the final chapter of a season in which Hamlin was consistently among the sport’s top contenders. Hamlin won Stage 2 and held the lead for long stretches before a late gamble sent him into the wall. Hamlin’s late gamble that sent him into the wall cost him several spots and ended his chance to win the title. Larson needed only to finish 28th or better to secure the crown, and he placed fourth in Stage 1 to clinch it early. A Season of Almost Hamlin refused to call his year a failure despite missing the ultimate prize. He told reporters after the race that the team’s effort was good and that he was proud of the Progressive Toyota team. He noted gains from Friday to the race and said he was happy with the effort put in on the racetrack. The numbers show a driver who was fast and consistent all year long. Hamlin completed all 36 races without a single DNF, a feat that is hard to pull off in a field of 39 other drivers. He led the most laps and won four events, proving his car was a championship machine. The problem was that championships are not given for good years. They are won by getting the job done on the very last Sunday of the season. The Final Gamble Hamlin admitted he was trying to win when he made the move that put him into the wall. He said he was just going for it at the end and that the move cost them some spots. He stated he definitely wanted to try to win and called it a fun race. The result left him seven points behind teammate Christopher Bell and 56 points behind Larson . Larson became the 11th driver in NASCAR Cup Series history to win at least three championships . He joins a group that includes three-time champions such as Tony Stewart, Joey Logano and Cale Yarborough, while Richard Petty and Jimmie Johnson remain tied for the all-time record with seven titles each. His crew chief, Cliff Daniels, became only the second man to win three championships in his first seven seasons. The victory for Hendrick Motorsports marks their 16th title , more than any other team in the sport.

The Middle Eastern conflict, which started in late February as the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran, has destabilised the region. The calendars of many motorsport championships have been impacted – not least F1’s, whose Saudi Arabian race was cancelled while Bahrain’s round was postponed and hosted in Malaysia. F1 has been monitoring the situation closely, with a Imola as an alternative season finale on the first weekend of December if Qatar and Abu Dhabi were unable to host their respective events. item.title: How Patriots can avoid placing Rhamondre Stevenson on IR after multi-week knee injury
item.description: How Patriots can avoid placing Rhamondre Stevenson on IR after multi-week knee injury originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The day after the New England Patriots were blown out by the Green Bay Packers , they got some bad news about running back Rhamondre Stevenson. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Stevenson is expected to "miss the next few weeks" due to a knee injury. New England will be without Stevenson for some time as he deals with this multi-week knee injury. However, even though Stevenson is set to miss some time, New England can avoid placing him on injured reserve. The reason why? It's all thanks to the team's well-timed Week 11 bye. How the Patriots can avoid putting Rhamondre Stevenson on IR "Patriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson is expected to miss the next few weeks because of a plantaris tendon issue in the back of his knee, sources say," Rapoport reports. "No surgery, just rest and rehab for Stevenson." For one, hearing that Stevenson doesn't need surgery is some great news. Surgery likely would've meant a lengthy absence, and a much more likely stint on IR. He is going to miss Week 10, which will make the Patriots' backfield thin, with the injury issue for TreVeyon Henderson as well. They could look to trade for an RB at the NFL trade deadline. But the good news for the Patriots is that with a Week 11 bye, they have a real chance to avoid placing Stevenson on IR, even if he does wind up not playing for four weeks. MORE : Mike Vrabel gives blunt assessment of Christian Gonzalez's struggles With Stevenson all but ruled out for Week 10, and the Patriots' Week 11 bye, Stevenson's status will be one to keep track of the team's next few games coming out of the bye. So long as the Patriots anticipate Stevenson coming back in Week 13 or Week 14, there is no reason to place him on IR. If he goes on IR, he would have to miss through at least Week 14, which would be quite the lengthy absence for an already thin RB room. Based on the "rest and rehab" prescription for Stevenson, however, it would make sense for the Patriots to get their top RB back in time in any of Weeks 12, 13, or 14, which would mean IR wouldn't need to be used. While the Patriots' RB room will be thin for Week 10, and maybe Week 12 as well, this update isn't all terrible, considering Stevenson doesn't need surgery, and there's no mention of him needing to go on IR. item.title: Bob Boone, 3-time All-Star and father of Yankees manager Aaron Boone, dies at 78
item.description: Bob Boone, the most accomplished member of a three-generation baseball family that's impacted Major League Baseball for the past 78 years, has died, according to his son, Bret. Boone was 78. The son of All-Star infielder Ray Boone and the father of current New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone and two-time All-Star Bret Boone, Bob Boone was a four-time All-Star catcher and star of the Philadelphia Phillies ' 1980 World Series champion team, the first in club history to win the Fall Classic. He played 19 years in the major leagues, moving on from Philadelphia to serve as the fulcrum of a California Angels squad that twice came within a game of the World Series, in 1982 and 1986. He finished his career with two seasons in Kansas City, retiring in 1990. Yet the family's story was only reaching its midpoint. After serving three years in the military during World War II, Ray Boone debuted on the last Cleveland team to win a World Series, in 1948. He enjoyed a 13-year career that included All-Star appearances in 1954 and '56. Yet just one month after Cleveland won the 1948 World Series, Ray's legacy would continue: Bob Boone was born in San Diego. Boone eventually attended Stanford and was a sixth-round pick of the Phillies in 1969. He'd reach the majors at 24, in 1972. Just two months before the Phillies drafted him, Boone's wife, Susan, gave birth to Bret Boone and Aaron would follow in 1973. Like their dad, Bret and Aaron were born in San Diego County and eventually grew up two hours north in Orange County as their dad became a veteran beacon for the Angels. He served as a manager for the Kansas City Royals from 1995-97 and the Cincinnati Reds from 2001-2003, managing Aaron for nearly three seasons in Cincinnati before the club traded him to the Yankees, where he'd hit his notorious pennant-winning home run in ALCS Game 7 later that year. At the 2002 All-Star Game in Miwaukee, the generations were united in most glorious fashion, Aaron representing the Reds as an NL All-Star, Bret repping the AL as a Seattle Mariner, both posing for photos with Bob and Ray, the first family to send three generations to a Midsummer Classic. Boone would continue in baseball, working in various capacities as a scout and special assistant, most notably in recent years with the Washington Nationals, earning a championship ring for their World Series title in 2019. Meanwhile, Aaron was named Yankees manager in 2018 and even as Bob stepped away from the game, he and Susan would watch Aaron's Yankees play from their home in California, according to Scott Miller's 2025 book Skipper. item.description: Germany's Niclas Fuellkrug speaks during a press conference ahead of Friday's UEFA Nations League soccer match against Serbia. (is associated with: «Füllkrug ready for much-awaited Germany comeback») Christian Charisius/dpa Forward Niclas Füllkrug is ready to make a much-awaited return to the Germany national football team a year and a half after his last international appearance. "We want to have guys who really want to play for Germany, who feel the national pride, who say they want to give that extra one per cent," the Werder Bremen player said in a news conference on Tuesday. "That's also what the coach exemplifies, what he stands for. Of course, you have a responsibility when you play for Germany. The country wants to see someone doing it with heart and passion." Füllkrug struggled in recent spells with West Ham and AC Milan due to injury and hasn't played for Germany since September 2025. But since returning to Bremen in August, he has scored 12 goals in 10 matches. He was overlooked for Jürgen Klopp's first squad, with the former Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool boss mentioning Füllkrug's age as a factor. But the forward's form has convinced Klopp to change his mind. Füllkrug is proud to have made it back into the squad and sees it as "also a confirmation and recognition" of his work. "It's great to be here in this group, to be able to train under Jürgen Klopp. I believe he's one of the greatest personalities we have in German football," he said. He already senses "a drastic change" in the national team, which has been restructured under Klopp. Füllkrug also knows perfectly his role. Behind Arsenal's Kai Havertz, the established striker, he is competing with young rivals like Eintracht Frankfurt's Younes Ebnoutalib for playing time in the two upcoming Nations League matches against Serbia and the Netherlands. For now, he doesn't want to look too far ahead and think about Euro 2028, when he would be 35 years old. "I'm not looking that far ahead. I'm happy to be able to convince people that I can be an alternative here," he said.

item.title: Drill of the Week: Fix Your Driver Swing Now
item.description: Quincy's Luke Welter drives off the first tee. The Quincy Presidents golf team hosted the Scituate Sailors at Granite Links Golf Club in Quincy on Monday, Oct. 5, 2026. Most golfers ruin their drive before the club even moves back. They pull the handle too far inside, which forces a bad swing path later. This common error leads to weak shots or slices that run into the woods. Adam Bazalgette of Scratch Golf Academy has a fix that changes how the club starts. His new drill uses a simple mental picture to keep the swing on track. The method is called the “Laser Light” takeaway . It asks players to keep that light pointing at the trail pocket or leg during the backswing. This trick stops the hands from taking over too early. It forces the arms and body to move together as one unit. How The Grip Changes The Swing Getting the setup right is the first step to making this work. The player must hold the driver with just the lead hand at first. Then, the trail hand goes flat in front of the shaft. This position puts the back of the trail fingers right against the grip. It creates a physical block that stops the club from swinging too far inside. From this spot, the palm lines up with the clubface. This helps the golfer feel exactly where they are aiming before the swing starts. Making a few slow moves in this grip builds the right muscle memory. It feels strange at first, but it teaches the body the correct path. The club cannot get whipped inside when the hand is locked in this spot. Why The Light Picture Works The drill gives a clear target for the backswing. Instead of thinking about complex angles, the golfer just follows the light. They start the swing and feel that imaginary beam point at their trail side. This keeps the club on a shallower plane that matches the driver. A flat club needs a flat path to hit the ball solidly. Many players let the light shine out to the side as they pull the club inside. This happens when the hands get too active, and the body stops moving. The fix is to let the arms and body work together. Focusing on the light pointing at the pocket keeps the connection strong. It stops the “over the top” move that causes so many bad shots. Bazalgette notes that this feel works well on the tee without deep thinking. The drill helps keep the arms and body connected as the club moves back. It is a simple adjustment that does not need extra gear. A golfer can try it with just the driver in hand. The key is to trust the feeling once the hands go back to the normal grip. Drills often look good in practice until a real ball appears. The old bad habits try to come back when the pressure is on. Players must commit to the feel and trust it when they hit real shots. item.title: ‘Australian fans have not moved on’: Michael Clarke joins Sandpapergate storm as pressure mounts on Cricket Australia
item.description: The controversy surrounding Australia's 2018 Sandpapergate scandal has taken another turn, with former captain Michael Clarke joining the growing chorus demanding that Cricket Australia (CA) reopen its investigation following Usman Khawaja's explosive revelations. Clarke believes Australian cricket fans have still not received the complete truth about the ball-tampering episode and said the issue would continue to haunt the game until the investigation was revisited. His comments come amid contrasting accounts from former teammates, with David Warner backing Khawaja's version, Mitchell Starc standing by the bowlers' earlier statement and CA chief executive Todd Greenberg ruling out another probe. “We haven’t moved on. Australian fans have not moved on. They can’t trust what’s real. They don’t know the truth – until this (investigation) gets reopened and the truth comes out,” Clarke said on 2DayFM’s Breakfast with Nath & Emma. Clarke wants the complete truth to emerge Khawaja reignited the debate through his forthcoming autobiography, Sabr, claiming that the entire Australian Test dressing room, including players and support staff, knew about the use of sandpaper during the 2018 tour of South Africa. The controversy first erupted during the third Test at Cape Town, where Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera attempting to alter the condition of the ball. Smith, Warner and Bancroft subsequently received suspensions, with the latter two also facing additional sanctions. Clarke said the opportunity to establish the complete truth had been missed in 2018 and again when Bancroft made comments about the involvement of other players in a 2021 interview with The Guardian. “We had the chance in 2018. The truth didn’t come out. We had the chance in 2021 when (Cameron Bancroft) made those comments (to The Guardian). The truth didn’t come out. Now we’ve got this opportunity. I would just like to see whatever the truth is for it all to come out, allow people to finally tell the truth, and move on,” he said. DeChambeau can apply for DP World Tour membership based on his status as a recent major champion, and that may offer him a route to regaining his PGA Tour card for 2028. McIlroy, who is preparing for the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai, last week backed claims that LIV Golf had sought to “destroy the European Tour”. “I think a name like Bryson DeChambeau and everything he brings with him, good and bad, he brings eyeballs, which is a good thing for tournaments,” said McIlroy, who was pipped to the 2024 US Open title by DeChambeau. Another Race to Dubai crown would draw him level with Colin Montgomerie, who won the European Tour's Order of Merit eight times, including seven consecutive titles between 1993 and 1999. The Northern Irishman trails Spain's Eugenio Chacarra by 533.93 points going into the final tournament of the season at Jumeirah Golf Estates, with 2,000 points available to the winner. He is among nine players in contention for the Race to Dubai title. “I’m very excited to be back here, very excited to be in contention for the eighth,” the world number two told reporters on Tuesday. “I made some ground up last week, maybe not as much as I wanted, but I felt like it was a step in the right direction.” McIlroy also expressed pride in the consistency he has maintained throughout his career. “I think this will be the 15th or 16th year in a row that I will have finished the year in the top 10 in the world rankings,” he said. “I’m very proud of that. item.title: Felix Nmecha responds to criticism of controversial Bundesliga goal celebration
item.description: Felix Nmecha responds to criticism of controversial Bundesliga goal celebration Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha has publicly addressed the controversy surrounding his recent goal celebration. In an Instagram statement reported by Sportschau , the German international rejected suggestions that his gesture was intended to promote discrimination or intolerance. “With my celebration, I wanted neither to put myself nor any organization in the foreground,” Nmecha explained. “Rather, it is about laying my ‘crown’ before the king who will soon return and pointing to Jesus — my hope and my strength.” The 26-year-old acknowledged that the gesture had attracted criticism and attempted to clarify its intended meaning. “I was informed that my recent goal celebration had led to some misunderstandings,” Nmecha wrote. “My message was never about spreading intolerance, discrimination, or hatred in any form.” Nmecha further emphasized that his Christian faith centered on love and respect for all people, irrespective of their backgrounds, beliefs, or worldviews. Klopp speaks with Nmecha as Dortmund plans further talks The Dortmund midfielder’s statement comes amid mounting criticism of a celebration resembling a gesture associated with the “The King’s Return” campaign, which has links to the evangelical network “Ballers in God.” Research conducted by German public broadcaster ARD’s Monitor programme uncovered discriminatory messaging associated with the campaign’s wider religious environment, including descriptions of homosexuality as a sin and abortion as Satan’s plan. Dortmund’s Fan and Supporters’ Department subsequently called for Nmecha to distance himself clearly from such evangelical networks , arguing that religious freedom should not be used to justify messages that undermine the dignity or equality of others. While Nmecha explicitly rejected discrimination and hatred in his latest statement, he did not directly distance himself from the organizations associated with the controversy. According to information obtained by dpa and reported by Sportschau , Germany national team head coach Jürgen Klopp has already discussed the matter with Nmecha at the national team’s headquarters in Herzogenaurach. Details of their conversation have not been disclosed. DFB sporting director Rudi Völler had also announced plans to speak with the player. Meanwhile, Borussia Dortmund’s management intends to hold further discussions with the midfielder, according to German news agency Sport-Informations-Dienst . Nmecha’s explanation represents his first direct public response to the latest criticism, although questions surrounding the religious networks associated with his celebration remain unresolved.
